agent_summary: The only real gap in this family is the VWF/ADAMTS13 axis: one small study (CB446, 12 dogs vs 10 controls) measured VWF in dogs with babesiosis, without a severity contrast, and no study has measured ADAMTS13. Canine assays exist for both (VWF:Ag ELISA, ADAMTS13 activity ELISA), but neither protein is a master protein in DS07, so testing needs stored plasma. Only DS06 has them, as whole-blood gene expression. Fibrinolytic shutdown (PAI-1, alpha-2-antiplasmin) and the anticoagulant pathway (antithrombin, protein C, thrombomodulin) have already been tested against severity: 2 and 4 independent units. Most of the 70 F4-04 keyword hits only mention DIC. Surprises: alpha-2-antiplasmin rose in survivors but not in non-survivors (CB145); PAI-1 and TAFI were low at admission in B. canis, so consumption, not shutdown (CB004); and soluble EPCR (added) was measured once in uncomplicated cases only.

mechanisms.human_direction: VWF antigen, VWF activity and ultra-large multimers higher in severe and cerebral malaria; ADAMTS13 activity lower, so the VWF/ADAMTS13 ratio is higher in severe disease

mechanisms.testable_detail: Not in DS07 (no master or candidate). DS06 has ENSCAFG00000015228_VWF and ENSCAFG00000019776_ADAMTS13, but this is whole-blood gene expression, a weak proxy (plasma VWF comes from endothelium and megakaryocytes, ADAMTS13 from the liver). A plasma test needs stored citrated plasma (VWF:Ag ELISA, ADAMTS13 activity ELISA).
mechanisms.notes: Canine VWF:Ag ELISAs are standard in von Willebrand disease testing; the validation (Can J Vet Res 2008, PMC2568046) has no DOI. ADAMTS13 has never been measured in canine babesiosis. In the one canine study, VWF fell (consumption?) where it rises in human malaria. The direction may differ between species.

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS06 has ENSCAFG00000015180_SELP and ENSCAFG00000031174_PPBP (whole-blood expression; platelet transcripts). DS07: PPBP J9P346 is master_candidate only (14% coverage), so it does not count. No soluble P-selectin or PF4 in DS02.
mechanisms.notes: Gap 'no' only because cell-surface CD62P was compared by outcome (CB504, CH03, 7 deaths). Soluble P-selectin and PF4/CXCL4 have never been measured in canine babesiosis, and no canine validation of a soluble assay was found. Human evidence is thin (grade 1).

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS07 masters: PLG F1Q421 (28%) and Q6JDI3 (17%), SERPINF2 E2R4V3 (26%); SERPINF2 A0A5F4CB96 is master_candidate. PAI-1 (SERPINE1) not in DS07. DS06 has SERPINE1 and SERPINF2 (expression).
mechanisms.notes: Canine-specific PAI-1 ELISA (CB004) and chromogenic alpha-2-AP activity (CB145) used. Directions conflict with the human 'shutdown' picture: in B. canis, PAI-1 is low at admission; in B. rossi, alpha-2-AP is high only in survivors. tPA-modified TEG has not been used in babesiosis.

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS07 masters: SERPINC1 E2RES2 (antithrombin-III, 18%) and PROC Q28278 (4% coverage, low); other PROC entries are master_candidate. THBD not in DS07 or DS06. DS06 has SERPINC1 (expression).
mechanisms.notes: Well covered: 4 independent units (CB438, CB145/CH03, CB004, CB112) compared AT, protein C or TM by severity. Protein C (CB438, CB112) and AT (CB145) are lower in severe or fatal disease. In CB438 AT did not differ, so AT results are mixed.

mechanisms.mechanism: Soluble endothelial protein C receptor (sEPCR) shedding
mechanisms.human_direction: sEPCR higher in severe and cerebral malaria and in children who died (Benin); higher and rising in non-survivors of pneumococcal septic shock (278 patients)

cb_confirmed.what: EPCR by canine-specific ELISA, 25 uncomplicated B. canis dogs vs 10 controls; only APC differed in the PC pathway

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS06 has ENSCAFG00000007945_PROCR (whole-blood expression, not shed plasma protein). Not found in DS07 B_Proteins.txt descriptions. Plasma sEPCR needs stored samples (canine ELISA as in CB011).
mechanisms.notes: Added because EPCR loss and shedding link coagulation to sequestration in falciparum malaria (PfEMP1 binds EPCR). No Babesia ligand for EPCR is known, so the transfer rests on sepsis-type shedding rather than parasite binding. The two Benin papers may share a cohort, so they are counted as one. 'Validated' rests on a canine-specific kit (CB011), not on a formal validation study.
